verdicts.trueWording: Each part gets one-to-two sentences; "This is Story Objective A."
verdicts.note: Overview template, DC Adventure Format v1.3 p.'Adventure Primer': Parts 1-4 each read "Each part of the adventure should have its own entry of one to two sentences describing the part. This is Story Objective A/B/C/D." A margin comment adds "Each part should have a Story Objective entry that describes the objective as a single sentence." Quote verbatim; both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: NPC Snapshot "is titled accordingly"; examples "Stoic Guardian", "Ruthless Conqueror"
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim. The NPC block is exactly as claimed: an opening paragraph giving "a brief glimpse into the NPC's backstory and physical appearance," then "What They Want. This single-sentence paragraph..." and "NPC Snapshot. This single-sentence paragraph... and is titled accordingly." The document states only that the Snapshot is retitled to suit the NPC; it never prescribes a length. Both worked examples happen to be two words, so "two-word" is induced from the examples, not a stated rule.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the epithet is specifically two words - the page says only "titled accordingly" and gives two examples that happen to be two words

verdicts.trueWording: Area Information entries: Dimensions and Terrain, Lighting, Sounds and Smells
verdicts.note: Quote "Dimensions and Terrain." appears twice - in the worked example under an Area Information heading (followed by Lighting) and in the margin comment "Area Information breaks down the area itself. There are usually three standard entries here: Dimensions and Terrain... Lighting... Sounds and Smells." Inline-subhead limb supported: "If under a heading 3, use inline subheads without the Area/Creature Information headings."

verdicts.trueWording: Creature names and keyed objects such as traps or secret doors are bold
verdicts.note: Quote "Use boldface judiciously." verbatim, in: "names of creatures or other significant game objects such as traps or secret doors are in bold. Use boldface judiciously. With the exception of creature names, it usually applies to important objects that are keyed on the map." Every limb supported, including the keyed-object restriction.

verdicts.trueWording: Sidebar gives background to help run the location; Playing the Pillars excepted
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim: "It should provide the DM with background information that may help run the location or event. With the exception of Playing the Pillars (see example, below), it shouldn't provide directly applicable information." The page's prohibition is on directly applicable *information*, which is broader than the claim's "rules content" and so entails it.

verdicts.trueWording: "Playing the Pillars. Suggestions for this encounter:" then Combat, Exploration, Social
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the worked encounter, followed by Combat / Exploration / Social entries. The optionality in "can carry" is supported by the margin comment "If you include this entry, each pillar of play should be represented" and "99% of the time, these entries should be under a Creature Information heading."

Quote verbatim. The cover block runs Adventure Title / Subtitle / description / "A Two/Four -Hour Adventure for Tier $ Characters." / "CONTENT WARNING: $", then the Credits list containing "Sensitivity Lead: TBD" among Writer, Editor, Graphic Design. File metadata confirms the 2023 dating: created 2023-11-07 by Claire Hoffman, last modified 2023-11-16 by Ma'at Crook.

verdicts.trueWording: Consult Chicago 17th; preferred dictionary Merriam-Webster's Collegiate 11th
verdicts.note: No quote was supplied with the claim, so the verbatim grade cannot apply; the substance is stated almost word for word on the first page: "Consult The Chicago Manual of Style (17th edition) if you have questions about punctuation, grammar, and other matters of writing style. Our preferred dictionary is Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary (11th edition)."

verdicts.trueWording: "This Boxed Text style is used only for text that a DM is meant to read to the players."
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the style-demonstration line of the .dotx. "Solely" matches the page's "only". Metadata confirms the source: dc:creator "Crawford, Jeremy", created 2019-09-30, modified 2019-10-08.

verdicts.trueWording: Unless excerpting a book where the quotes appear in the original
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim: "An epigraph shouldn't be enclosed in quotation marks, unless you're excerpting a passage from a book and the quotes appear in the original." Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "If it must immediately follow something, don't make it a sidebar; integrate it into the body copy."
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim under Sidebar Body: "ask yourself whether the sidebar must immediately follow a section of text or whether it can go anywhere on a spread. If it must immediately follow something, don't make it a sidebar; integrate it into the body copy." Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: "Profanity. Don't use profanity." plus "not without approval"
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim in the standards list. The approval carve-out limb is supported by the RATING section: "D&D products can violate certain standards, but not without approval," and "PG-rated content allows things we normally don't, such as nudity and profanity."

verdicts.trueWording: G-rated, slides toward PG; Rick & Morty PG-13 needed approval
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim. Every limb on the page: "When it deals with mature themes or features scenes of graphic violence, it slides toward being a PG-rated experience" and "The Rick & Morty boxed set, which contains profanity and glamorizes substance abuse, is an example of just such a product. It is rated PG-13," following "can violate certain standards, but not without approval."

verdicts.trueWording: "...to all members of a particular people, culture, religion, or sexuality."
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim under the Stereotypes standard, which opens "Avoid stereotypes." All four categories in the claim appear on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: "Villains can be sympathetic, but their evil should be called out as awful and wrong. Avoid depicting evil heroes."
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim under Glamorization of Evil. Both limbs on the page, including the evil-heroes limb.
